-- Converted: CREATE SET TABLE -> CREATE TABLE; sales.customer -> SALES.CUSTOMER (naming map); removed PRIMARY INDEX (customer_id); column definitions kept as written
-- Reason: Snowflake has no SET / PRIMARY INDEX syntax. Micro-partitioning replaces Teradata hash distribution, and a clustering key is only worth adding for large tables after measuring. Column types, NOT NULL and DEFAULT are valid Snowflake syntax as written
CREATE TABLE SALES.CUSTOMER (
  customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  customer_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
  status CHAR(1) DEFAULT 'A'
);

unsupported: SET table semantics (Teradata silently rejects duplicate rows): Snowflake tables always allow duplicates (MULTISET behaviour). Load processes must de-duplicate if they relied on this.

PRIMARY INDEX (customer_id): Snowflake has no primary-index/hash-distribution concept. It is dropped, not turned into CLUSTER BY, to stay literal; add ALTER TABLE SALES.CUSTOMER CLUSTER BY (customer_id) later if the table is large and filtered on these columns.

assumptions: INTEGER and BIGINT are kept as written; in Snowflake both are synonyms for NUMBER(38,0), so the value range is wider than Teradata's 32-bit/64-bit integers (the type map lists no direct equivalent). Existing data fits without loss.
Schema SALES exists in the target database, and the current database is set when the script runs.
ACCOUNT is a Snowflake reserved keyword, so the table name is double-quoted as SALES."ACCOUNT" (uppercase), as the naming map specifies. Every reference must use the same quoted, uppercase name.

The inline REFERENCES constraint is kept as in the source and points to SALES.CUSTOMER from the naming map. Snowflake records the foreign key but does not enforce it (only NOT NULL is enforced), so referential integrity must be checked in ETL.

SALES.CUSTOMER is created first (dependency order). The source does not declare a PRIMARY KEY/UNIQUE constraint on customer_id, and Teradata also expects one on the referenced column. If Snowflake rejects the foreign key because the parent has no primary/unique key, add a PRIMARY KEY (customer_id) on SALES.CUSTOMER or remove the REFERENCES clause.
explanations: CREATE MULTISET TABLE becomes CREATE TABLE SALES."ACCOUNT", using the naming-map name.
Columns, data types, NOT NULL, DEFAULT values and column order are unchanged.
